Method coefficients

Source: vignettes/articles/methods-coefficients.Rmd
methods-coefficients.Rmd

Coefficients and sources of the four methods of Stepping and error control, selected by method and useNDF of cppODE(). Symbols follow the notation table.

BDF and NDF coefficients

Source. Shampine and Reichelt [1], Table 1; implemented in cppde_multistepper.hpp.

The NDF of order \(q\) adds to the BDF\(q\) corrector a term proportional to the Nordsieck predictor error, \[ \sum_{m=1}^{q} \frac{1}{m}\, \nabla^{m} x_{n+1} \;-\; h_n\, f(x_{n+1}, t_{n+1}) \;-\; \kappa_q\, H_q\, \bigl(x_{n+1} - x_{n+1}^{\mathrm{pred}}\bigr) \;=\; 0, \qquad H_q \;=\; \sum_{m=1}^{q} \tfrac{1}{m}, \tag{1} \] with \(\nabla\) the backward-difference operator; \(\kappa_q = 0\) gives BDF\(q\). useNDF (default TRUE) selects NDF or BDF at compile time.

NDF coefficients \(\kappa_q\) of cppDE, empirical step-size gain over BDF\(q\) at matched local error, and stability angle. NDF5 is BDF5, since the BDF5 angle of \(51^\circ\) leaves no room for reduction.
\(q\) \(\kappa_q\) step-size gain over BDF\(q\) stability angle
1 -0.1850 \(+26\,\%\) A-stable
2 -0.1111 \(+26\,\%\) A-stable
3 -0.0823 \(+26\,\%\) \(80^\circ\)
4 -0.0415 \(+12\,\%\) \(66^\circ\)
5 0.0000 \(0\,\%\) \(51^\circ\) (\(=\) BDF5)

Adams-Moulton coefficients

Source. Hindmarsh et al. [2], the \(\ell\)-vector formulation of CVODE; implemented in cppde_multistepper.hpp by adams_set_coefficients().

The coefficients depend on the past step sizes and are recomputed every step. With \(\xi_j = (t_{n+1} - t_{n+1-j})/h_n\), the correction vector \((\ell_0, \dots, \ell_q)\) of the Nordsieck array holds the coefficients of the polynomial \(\Lambda(u) = \sum_{j=0}^{q} \ell_j u^j\) with \[ \Lambda(-1) \;=\; 0, \qquad \Lambda(0) \;=\; 1, \qquad \Lambda'(u) \;\propto\; \prod_{j=1}^{q-1} \bigl(1 + u/\xi_j\bigr), \] and the weight of the implicit term is \(\beta_0 = 1/\ell_1\). At constant step size the corrector weights \(\beta_0, \dots, \beta_q\) are the fixed-step values of [3], Table III.1.1. The controller selects \(q \in \{1, \dots, 12\}\); \(q_{\max} = 12\) is the CVODE default.

Rosenbrock4 coefficients

Source. Hairer and Wanner [4, Sec. IV.7], the default coefficients of the rosenbrock4 stepper of Boost.Numeric.Odeint except the sign of \(d_4\), which is that of rodas.f; implemented in default_rosenbrock_coefficients in cppde_rosenbrock4.hpp.

With \(W = (\gamma h_n)^{-1} I - J(x_n, t_n)\), the stage equations are \[ \begin{aligned} W\, k_i &\;=\; f\!\left(x_n + \sum_{j<i} \alpha_{ij}\, k_j,\; t_n + c_i\, h_n \right) \;+\; \frac{1}{h_n} \sum_{j<i} \gamma_{ij}\, k_j \;+\; h_n\, d_i\, \frac{\partial f}{\partial t}, \\ x_{n+1} &\;=\; x_n + \sum_{i=1}^{s} m_i\, k_i, \qquad \hat x_{n+1} \;=\; x_n + \sum_{i=1}^{s} \hat m_i\, k_i. \end{aligned} \] cppDE uses \(s = 6\) and \(\gamma = 1/4\), indexed as in the source.

The sixth stage, at the embedded order-\(3\) solution \(X_6\), is the error estimate \(e_{n+1}\), which the step solution adds to \(X_6\): \[ X_6 \;=\; x_n + \sum_{i=1}^{5} \alpha_{6,i}\, k_i, \qquad W\, e_{n+1} \;=\; f(X_6,\, t_n + h_n) + \frac{1}{h_n}\sum_{i=1}^{5} \gamma_{6,i}\, k_i, \qquad x_{n+1} \;=\; X_6 + e_{n+1}, \] with the sixth-row coefficients

Tsitouras 5(4) coefficients

Source. Tsitouras [5], Table 1 and eqs. (7), (8); implemented in cppde_tsit5.hpp.

The pair has \(s = 7\) stages and satisfies the first column simplifying assumption \(\sum_i b_i a_{ij} = b_j(1 - c_j)\) for every \(j\), but not the row condition \(\sum_j a_{ij} c_j = c_i^2/2\). The seventh stage is the FSAL stage: row \(a_{7,j}\) equals \(b_j\) for \(j = 1, \dots, 6\).

\(k_7 = f(x_{n+1},\, t_n + h_n)\) is \(k_1\) of step \(n+1\). With \(b_7 = 0\) and \(\hat b_7 \neq 0\), it enters the order-\(4\) estimate only. The controller uses \[ e_{n+1} \;=\; h_n \sum_{i=1}^{7} (\hat b_i - b_i)\, k_i. \]
